title: soft-retry-on-schema-validation-failures-for-streaming-responses
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customer-facing teams observed hard failures when streaming responses failed final JSON schema validation under strict mode. This caused production regressions for mixed workloads (tool-calling + structured output) and blocked rollouts of newer response_format variants. Motivation: provide a non-disruptive operational path that preserves stream stability while enforcing schema contracts where possible. Goals: (1) emit validation diagnostics inline with the stream instead of silently aborting in non-strict mode, (2) introduce a retryable validation category so transient formatting glitches can be fixed automatically or by the downstream client, and (3) keep OpenAI-compat param mappings intact for existing customers.

What's changed (high level): added a soft-retry path to streaming response validation that classifies validation failures into two buckets: RETRYABLE_SCHEMA (e.g., truncated JSON, unclosed arrays, missing trailing commas) and FATAL_SCHEMA (schema mismatch like wrong types for required fields). In non-strict mode (default for hosted API), a RETRYABLE_SCHEMA will cause the runtime to: (a) emit a new inline event type "validation_hint" with an id and short machine-readable diagnostic, (b) attempt up to two automatic repairs by requesting the model to reemit the last chunk with a corrected delimiter/closing token (this uses the existing stream control channel), and (c) if repairs fail, include the partial best-effort JSON in a final envelope with a validation status field so integrators can decide how to handle the payload. In strict mode the behavior is unchanged (validation failure => stream rejection).

Compatibility notes: added translation in the OpenAI-compat layer so response_format values "openai_json_schema" and "response_schema_v3" map to the new v3 schema negotiation. The compat mapping also exposes a boolean flag "strict": true|false. Default remains strict=false for the hosted product to reduce customer breakage, but enterprise Dedicated templates can opt-in to strict mode via config. The new behavior is gated behind a feature flag 'stream_schema_soft_retry' for controlled rollout.

Testing: end-to-end tests added in eval-harness and redwood-integration tests exercising tool-calling + schema streaming scenarios, including simulated model truncation, delayed tokens, and injected bad tokens. Unit tests cover the diagnostic format and automatic-repair logic. Load tests show <2% extra latency for repair attempts under typical 95th percentile workloads.

Operational impact: added metrics: schema.validation.attempts, schema.validation.retries, schema.validation.final_status (ok/repaired/fatal), and tracing annotations on stream control messages. Updated docs and SDKs to document the inline "validation_hint" event and the final envelope shape.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation - streaming validator + repair orchestration - [x] OpenAI compat mapping - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Metrics and traces - [x] Docs and SDK updates - [x] Feature flag for staged rollout

review_conversation:
Diego: Can the repair loop be re-entrant if model starts emitting infinite partial arrays?
Maya: We cap repairs to 2 attempts and enforce maximum emitted chunk length; added guard to stream_controller.go lines 184-212.
Priya: We need a clear machine-readable code for the hint so SDKs can map to retry behavior.
Maya: Introduced codes VSCHEMA-RETRYABLE and VSCHEMA-FATAL; added them to sdk enums and docs.
Samir: Integration tests flaked on CI initially due to timing; turns out we needed to wait for stream-control ACK. Fixed by adding a small jitter and explicit ACK in harness.
Diego: LGTM after addressing comments. Approved at 2026-03-02.

release_notes: Introduce soft-retry for streaming JSON schema validation: emits inline validation_hint events for retryable failures and attempts automatic repairs. Default non-strict behavior reduces hard stream rejections. Feature gated behind 'stream_schema_soft_retry'. SDKs and docs updated.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature flag enabled false by default in prod. Suggested staged enablement: 10% accounts -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring on schema.validation.retries and schema.validation.final_status metrics.
